other_aliases: the Holy One, blessed be He
relations.note: The Shekhinah is YHWH’s dwelling and manifest presence.

other_aliases: the Holy One, blessed be He
relations.myth: Separation and reunion of the Bride and Holy King
relations.note: The feminine Shekhinah separates from and reunites with the Holy King.
Kabbalah identifies the Shekhinah with the tenth and lowest sefirah.

relations.myth: Sabbath union of Malkhut and Tiferet
relations.note: Tiferet is her bridegroom; sin separates them and commandments restore their union.

relations.myth: Transmission of generative influx into Malkhut
relations.note: Yesod channels masculine generative influx into Shekhinah in a frequently sexualized relationship.
The lower Shekhinah is portrayed as Binah’s reflection within upper-lower Shekhinah schemes.
Late texts make Metatron her garment, vehicle, embodiment, or lower-world analogue, not an unqualified identity.

relations.myth: Captivity of Shekhinah by the other side
relations.note: Samael exploits her separation from holiness; restored divine union defeats or excludes his influence.

relations.myth: Demonic rivalry during the Shekhinah’s exile
relations.note: Lilith is her inverted rival; sexual sin strengthens Lilith while holy union restores the Shekhinah.

relations.myth: Friday-evening entrance and wedding of the Bride
relations.note: The personified Sabbath is identified with Shekhinah, who enters and reunites with the King.
Modern comparative systems equate their feminine emanation and restoration imagery despite independent ancient traditions.
Later Christian interpretations identify both with divine presence or a feminine aspect of divinity.
